source.original_text: Algorithm 3.1 draws a fresh standard Gaussian Z independently of the incoming phase state (X,Pinit) and forms P0=exp(-h/2)Pinit+sqrt(1-exp(-h))Z. For h>=0 and any incoming probability law with integrable combined squared state bounded by M, the refreshed combined moment equals the incoming position plus exp(-h) times incoming momentum moment, plus (1-exp(-h))d, and is at most M+(1-exp(-h))d. This is only the first half-refresh; the repeated history and D.7 remain separate.

lean.statement: For every complete finite-dimensional real-inner-product Borel space E, incoming probability law ν on E×E, xstar∈E, h>=0, and integrable incoming energy with integral at most M, under μ=ν.prod(stdGaussian E), X((x,p),z)=x, and P0((x,p),z)=exp(-h/2)p+sqrt(1-exp(-h))z are measurable, their combined squared energy is integrable, its integral equals the damped incoming integral plus (1-exp(-h))*finrank(E), and it is bounded by M plus that Gaussian term.

blind_reconstruction.text:
Let E be a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space equipped with its Borel σ-algebra, let ν be a probability measure on E × E, let x⋆ ∈ E, let h ∈ ℝ satisfy h ≥ 0, and let M ∈ ℝ. Assume the incoming energy (x,p) ↦ ‖x − x⋆‖² + ‖p‖² is ν-integrable and
∫_{E×E} (‖x − x⋆‖² + ‖p‖²) dν(x,p) ≤ M.
Let γ_E = stdGaussian(E), set μ = ν ⊗ γ_E, and for ((x,p),z) ∈ (E × E) × E define
X((x,p),z) = x,  P₀((x,p),z) = e^(−h/2)p + √(1 − e^(−h)) z.
Then X and P₀ are measurable, the function ((x,p),z) ↦ ‖X((x,p),z) − x⋆‖² + ‖P₀((x,p),z)‖² is μ-integrable, and
∫_{(E×E)×E} (‖X((x,p),z) − x⋆‖² + ‖P₀((x,p),z)‖²) dμ((x,p),z)
= ∫_{E×E} (‖x − x⋆‖² + e^(−h)‖p‖²) dν(x,p) + (1 − e^(−h)) finrank_ℝ(E)
≤ M + (1 − e^(−h)) finrank_ℝ(E).

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.StdGaussianMoment
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Prod
import Mathlib.Tactic

/-!
# The first partial momentum refresh in Smoothed Picard HMC

Algorithm 3.1 of Chen--Chewi--Lu--Zhang, arXiv:2609.06906v1, starts each
phase by adjoining a fresh standard Gaussian and setting

`P₀ = exp (-h / 2) P_init + sqrt (1 - exp (-h)) Z`.

The product measure below is the actual independence semantics of that draw.
The theorem proves the exact combined second-moment identity, including the
Gaussian dimension term suppressed in the short proof of Lemma D.4.  Thus an
incoming budget `M` becomes `M + (1 - exp (-h)) d`; it is not silently reused
unchanged.

The repeated Algorithm 3.1 history, its run-wide moment estimate, the second
momentum refresh, the Picard Gaussian array, and the numerical conclusion
(D.7) remain separate.
-/

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory InnerProductSpace
open scoped ENNReal RealInnerProductSpace

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.PartialMomentumRefresh

open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.StdGaussianMoment

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [CompleteSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]

/-- The actual independent Gaussian half-refresh has an exact second-moment
identity and supplies the corrected state budget needed by the first Picard
layer. -/
theorem partial_momentum_refresh_second_moment
    (ν : Measure (E × E)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (xstar : E) {h M : ℝ} (hh : 0 ≤ h)
    (hstateI : Integrable (fun s : E × E => ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖s.2‖ ^ 2) ν)
    (hstate : (∫ s : E × E, ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 ∂ν) ≤ M) :
    let a := Real.exp (-h / 2)
    let sigma := Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h))
    let μ := ν.prod (stdGaussian E)
    let X : (E × E) × E → E := fun w => w.1.1
    let P0 : (E × E) × E → E := fun w => a • w.1.2 + sigma • w.2
    Measurable X ∧ Measurable P0 ∧
      Integrable (fun w => ‖X w - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖P0 w‖ ^ 2) μ ∧
      (∫ w, ‖X w - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖P0 w‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) =
        (∫ s : E × E, ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + Real.exp (-h) * ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 ∂ν) +
          (1 - Real.exp (-h)) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) ∧
      (∫ w, ‖X w - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖P0 w‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) ≤
        M + (1 - Real.exp (-h)) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  have hexp : Real.exp (-h) ≤ 1 := Real.exp_le_one_iff.mpr (by linarith)
  have hvar : 0 ≤ 1 - Real.exp (-h) := sub_nonneg.mpr hexp
  have ha2 : Real.exp (-h / 2) ^ 2 = Real.exp (-h) := by
    rw [pow_two, ← Real.exp_add]
    congr 1
    ring
  have hs2 : Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h)) ^ 2 = 1 - Real.exp (-h) :=
    Real.sq_sqrt hvar
  have hposI : Integrable (fun s : E × E => ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2) ν := by
    apply hstateI.mono' (by fun_prop)
    filter_upwards with s
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (sq_nonneg _)]
    exact le_add_of_nonneg_right (sq_nonneg _)
  have hmomI : Integrable (fun s : E × E => ‖s.2‖ ^ 2) ν := by
    apply hstateI.mono' (by fun_prop)
    filter_upwards with s
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (sq_nonneg _)]
    exact le_add_of_nonneg_left (sq_nonneg _)
  have hmom1 : Integrable (fun s : E × E => s.2) ν :=
    MemLp.integrable (by norm_num : 1 ≤ (2 : ℝ≥0∞))
      ((memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq_norm (by fun_prop)).2 hmomI)
  obtain ⟨hgaussI, hgauss⟩ :=
    integrable_norm_sq_and_integral_stdGaussian (E := E)
  have hz1 : Integrable (fun z : E => z) (stdGaussian E) := IsGaussian.integrable_id
  have hcross : Integrable
      (fun w : (E × E) × E => inner ℝ w.1.2 w.2) (ν.prod (stdGaussian E)) :=
    hmom1.op_fst_snd (by fun_prop)
      ⟨1, by intro x y; simpa using norm_inner_le_norm (𝕜 := ℝ) x y⟩ hz1
  have hcross0 :
      (∫ w : (E × E) × E, inner ℝ w.1.2 w.2 ∂ν.prod (stdGaussian E)) = 0 := by
    rw [integral_prod _ hcross]
    have hz (s : E × E) :
        (∫ z : E, inner ℝ s.2 z ∂stdGaussian E) = 0 :=
      integral_strongDual_stdGaussian (innerSL ℝ s.2)
    simp only [hz, integral_zero]
  have hposP := hposI.comp_fst (stdGaussian E)
  have hmomP := hmomI.comp_fst (stdGaussian E)
  have hgaussP := hgaussI.comp_snd ν
  have hcrossC : Integrable (fun w : (E × E) × E =>
      (2 * Real.exp (-h / 2) * Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h))) *
        inner ℝ w.1.2 w.2) (ν.prod (stdGaussian E)) := hcross.const_mul _
  have hbase : Integrable (fun w : (E × E) × E =>
      ‖w.1.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + Real.exp (-h) * ‖w.1.2‖ ^ 2)
      (ν.prod (stdGaussian E)) := hposP.add (hmomP.const_mul _)
  have hbaseCross : Integrable (fun w : (E × E) × E =>
      ‖w.1.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + Real.exp (-h) * ‖w.1.2‖ ^ 2 +
        (2 * Real.exp (-h / 2) * Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h))) *
          inner ℝ w.1.2 w.2) (ν.prod (stdGaussian E)) := hbase.add hcrossC
  have hnoiseC : Integrable (fun w : (E × E) × E =>
      (1 - Real.exp (-h)) * ‖w.2‖ ^ 2) (ν.prod (stdGaussian E)) :=
    hgaussP.const_mul _
  have hpieces : Integrable (fun w : (E × E) × E =>
      ‖w.1.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + Real.exp (-h) * ‖w.1.2‖ ^ 2 +
        (2 * Real.exp (-h / 2) * Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h))) *
          inner ℝ w.1.2 w.2 +
        (1 - Real.exp (-h)) * ‖w.2‖ ^ 2) (ν.prod (stdGaussian E)) :=
    hbaseCross.add hnoiseC
  have hexpand (w : (E × E) × E) :
      ‖w.1.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 +
          ‖Real.exp (-h / 2) • w.1.2 +
            Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h)) • w.2‖ ^ 2 =
        ‖w.1.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + Real.exp (-h) * ‖w.1.2‖ ^ 2 +
          (2 * Real.exp (-h / 2) * Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h))) *
            inner ℝ w.1.2 w.2 +
          (1 - Real.exp (-h)) * ‖w.2‖ ^ 2 := by
    rw [norm_add_sq_real, norm_smul, norm_smul, real_inner_smul_left,
      real_inner_smul_right]
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos (Real.exp_pos _),
      abs_of_nonneg (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)]
    simp only [mul_pow, ha2, hs2]
    ring
  have houtI : Integrable (fun w : (E × E) × E =>
      ‖w.1.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 +
        ‖Real.exp (-h / 2) • w.1.2 +
          Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h)) • w.2‖ ^ 2)
      (ν.prod (stdGaussian E)) := by
    simpa only [hexpand] using hpieces
  have heq :
      (∫ w : (E × E) × E,
          ‖w.1.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 +
            ‖Real.exp (-h / 2) • w.1.2 +
              Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h)) • w.2‖ ^ 2
          ∂ν.prod (stdGaussian E)) =
        (∫ s : E × E,
          ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + Real.exp (-h) * ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 ∂ν) +
          (1 - Real.exp (-h)) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) := by
    simp_rw [hexpand]
    rw [integral_add hbaseCross hnoiseC,
      integral_add hbase hcrossC,
      integral_const_mul, hcross0, mul_zero, add_zero,
      integral_const_mul, integral_prod _ hgaussP]
    simp only [hgauss, integral_const]
    rw [integral_prod _ hbase]
    simp only [integral_const]
    simp
  have hweighted :
      (∫ s : E × E,
          ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + Real.exp (-h) * ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 ∂ν) ≤ M := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ∫ s : E × E, ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 ∂ν := by
        apply integral_mono (hposI.add (hmomI.const_mul _)) hstateI
        intro s
        change ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + Real.exp (-h) * ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 ≤
          ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖s.2‖ ^ 2
        have hp : Real.exp (-h) * ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 ≤ ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 := by
          simpa only [one_mul] using
            mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hexp (sq_nonneg ‖s.2‖)
        exact add_le_add_right hp (‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2)
      _ ≤ M := hstate
  refine ⟨by fun_prop, by fun_prop, houtI, heq, ?_⟩
  rw [heq]
  linarith

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.PartialMomentumRefresh

assumptions: The incoming phase-state law nu on E×E is a probability measure, and the combined square ‖X−x*‖²+‖Pinit‖² is integrable with expectation at most M.

lesson.statement: Set a=exp(−h/2), sigma=sqrt(1−exp(−h)), X0=X and P0=a Pinit+sigma Z on the product law of the incoming state and a fresh standard Gaussian. Then X0 and P0 are measurable, their combined squared distance is integrable, and its expectation satisfies the exact identity and corrected budget below.

steps.title: Realize the fresh draw by a product law
steps.text: A sample is a pair ((X,Pinit),Z) distributed according to nu⊗gamma_d. The first coordinate is the incoming phase state and the second is a genuinely fresh standard Gaussian. Coordinate projections and continuous linear combinations make X0 and P0 measurable.
steps.lean: The public X and P0 lets use product projections; the final fun_prop goals prove their measurability.

steps.title: Establish every integrability premise
steps.text: Nonnegativity lets us extract the position and momentum square integrability from the combined incoming energy. L2 then gives integrability of Pinit itself. The shared ASTIS theorem gives ‖Z‖² in L1, while Mathlib's Gaussian integrability API separately gives Z in L1; together these make the mixed inner product integrable on the product measure.
steps.formula: \|X-x_*\|^2,\|P_{\rm init}\|^2\in L^1(\nu),\quad P_{\rm init}\in L^1(\nu),\quad Z,\|Z\|^2\in L^1(\gamma_d).
steps.lean: hposI, hmomI, hmom1, hgaussI, hz1 and Integrable.op_fst_snd justify Fubini and all subsequent integral algebra.

steps.title: Use actual independence to kill the cross term
steps.text: For every fixed incoming momentum, the Gaussian mean is zero. Fubini is legal because the mixed inner product was proved integrable, hence its expectation under the product law vanishes without a centering assumption on Pinit.
steps.formula: \mathbb E_{\nu\otimes\gamma_d}\langle P_{\rm init},Z\rangle=\mathbb E_\nu\langle P_{\rm init},\mathbb E_{\gamma_d}Z\rangle=0.

steps.title: Expand the refreshed square
steps.text: The coefficients satisfy a²=e^(−h) and sigma²=1−e^(−h). Expanding the Hilbert norm, integrating the four integrable terms, using the zero cross term and E‖Z‖²=d gives the exact identity.
steps.lean: ha2, hs2, hexpand, hpieces and heq mirror this algebra and product integration.

steps.title: Derive the consumer-ready bound
steps.text: Because h≥0, 0<e^(−h)≤1. Replacing the damped momentum term by the incoming momentum square and applying the input budget yields M+(1−e^(−h))d. The extra dimension term must remain visible until the later paper-parameter absorption step.
steps.lean: hexp, hweighted and heq prove the final inequality. The focused test passes this result to picard_center_gradient_moment.

lesson.lean_statement: The source's independent Gaussian draw is represented definitionally by a product measure. The conclusion exposes measurability and integrability because the next Picard theorem requires them, and keeps Pinit distinct from the refreshed P0.
lesson.lean_proof: ASTIS supplies the canonical Gaussian norm-square leaf and the paper-specific product-law adapter. Mathlib supplies product Fubini, Gaussian mean/covariance, Lp-to-integrability and Hilbert norm algebra.
